editorial_intent: Diagram how the loss of transcription factor SRF degrades smooth muscle cell contractile machinery and causes collecting lymphatic vessels to dilate without cell death.
subject: A split longitudinal cross-section of a collecting lymphatic vessel comparing a tightly wrapped, actively contracting smooth muscle wall with densely packed actin-myosin filaments against an aged, dilated vessel wall with intact but slack, non-functional smooth muscle cells whose inner contractile fibers have dissolved into sparse fragments.
setting: A background grid woven with a hexagonal fourth-phase water crystal lattice, concentric hydration shells, and four laminar drainage sluice vectors that direct fluid movement.
composition: Asymmetric Post-Constructivist dual-panel lithograph layout with a left-to-right temporal progression, featuring sharp diagonal vector overlays in terracotta oxide and dynamic tension lines in burnt saffron framing the central lymphatic cylinder.
